Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

mutual adjective

also mutually, reciprocal, shared (mutual), the feeling is mutual

classical

Cic. Fam. 13.65.1: officia (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 30.30.2: admīrātiōne mūtuā
Traupman 349

mūtuus, mūtua, mūtuum

declension

mutual, in return

Its first sense is “lent, borrowed”: pecūniās mūtuās sūmere, to borrow money (Cic. Phil. 10.26); then, given and returned, on both sides.

Other words

  • mūtuō — mutually, in return

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 4.1.1; Planc. ap. Cic. Fam. 10.15.4: mē mūtuō dīligās (Lewis & Short)

    “The same back”: mūtuō mehercule, “and we feel the same, truly”. With a verb, inter sē often does the work (see each other).

Examples

  • paulisper alter alterīus cōnspectū, admīrātiōne mūtuā prope attonitī, conticuēre

    for a little while, each at the sight of the other, almost stunned with mutual admiration, they fell silentLiv. 30.30.2

  • cupis post longum tempus neptem tuam mēque ūnā vidēre. grātum est utrīque nostrum quod cupis, mūtuō mehercule

    you long to see your granddaughter, and me with her, after so long. We are both glad that you do, and truly, the feeling is mutualPlin. Ep. 4.1.1

See also each other, in turn.
